checkpoints.description: [1/4] Plan: height-fit the 23-row Confluence on phones at a 24px cell floor, keeping the page-scroll fallback when the floor cannot fit

impact_assessment.why: At 390x844 the Confluence board is 340x711 starting at y=264 and ending at 974, 130px below the fold; at 320x568 it ends at 867, 299px below. The player cannot see both ends of the relay while solving, and the 24px floor is already guaranteed by the README.
impact_assessment.benefits: At 390 the whole 11x23 relay fits in the viewport at about 24px cells; at 320 the board keeps 24px cells and the existing page scroll remains the fallback. Normal and wide boards keep their current sizing.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: compact fit path gains a height branch; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: no save change; layout: the tall frame becomes 283px wide at 390, leaving whitespace, and the game foot may sit just below the fold.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Pure fitBoardWidth mobile cases, 390/320 before/after measurements, a played Confluence clear at 390 and 320, desktop regression geometry and the 18-level run.

[1/4] Plan: compact the phone chamber index with episode tabs that show one episode at a time, leaving desktop unchanged

impact_assessment.why: The chamber index is 5,224px tall at 390 and 5,359px at 320 because all four episodes and eighteen cards stack in one column. The player must scroll through locked episodes to reach the current one.
impact_assessment.benefits: A four-tab episode filter shows one episode grid at a time on phones, cutting the initial page by most of the other three episodes while keeping every chamber and the progress bar. Desktop keeps all episodes visible.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: adds episode-tabs and episode-tab controls plus active-episode state; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: UI-only tab selection, no save change; layout: tabs scroll horizontally at 320 if labels overflow, and hidden blocks stay in the DOM.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Pure nextEpisodeId cases for fresh, partially completed and complete progress, a 44px tab target, before/after heights at 390/320, a played Episode II tab and Double Down clear, desktop all-episode regression and the 18-level run.

[1/4] Plan: add a one-step-history Undo action that reverts the last rotation, refunds its move and keeps the star pace correct

impact_assessment.why: The game has restart but no undo, so a single mistap on a 24-28px mobile cell forces a full chamber restart or a worse star score. Puzzle players expect undo, and touch boards make it more important.
impact_assessment.benefits: Undo restores the previous piece orientation, decrements moves, clears transient effects and re-renders the beam; a HUD button, Z shortcut and accessible label make it reachable without restarting.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: session gains a rotation history and a new data-ui control; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: history is in-memory only, no save change; layout: a third HUD icon must fit at 390 and wrap cleanly at 320.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Engine tests for undo restore/refund/empty/reset, a mobile 390/320 HUD measurement, a real misrotation-then-undo played run with star-pace restoration, keyboard Z proof and the 18-level regression.

Task 'undo-move' completed successfully.
[1/4] Plan: confirm a chamber restart once the run has at least one move, so the restart icon cannot wipe progress on a single mobile mistap

impact_assessment.why: The restart icon sits directly beside the new undo icon in the phone HUD. A mistap currently resets all rotations immediately, while undo only protects the last rotation. Puzzle runs can be 13 moves, so accidental loss is costly.
impact_assessment.benefits: After the first move, reset asks for confirmation with the chamber name and move count; Keep playing closes the dialog with the board intact, and Restart chamber resets. A zero-move restart stays immediate, and the pause dialog's deliberate restart is unchanged.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: adds a restart modal kind and a hints helper; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: no save change; layout: the existing dialog is reused, so no new layout surface.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Pure restartPrompt cases for singular/plural/fallback, a mobile played probe for one move then Cancel then confirm, a keyboard R probe, a zero-move immediate reset, the 18-level regression and the full gates.

checkpoints.description: [2/4] Implemented: restartPrompt helper with three tests, requestReset guard on HUD and R after the first move, Keep playing primary, direct zero-move reset, pause restart unchanged, README and ADR-031

Task 'restart-confirm' completed successfully.
[1/5] Plan: add a deterministic Daily Relay on the title screen with its own saved result and streak, leaving campaign progress untouched

impact_assessment.why: The game has 18 handcrafted chambers but no reason to return after they are cleared. The earlier store analysis flagged the missing retention hook; a daily chamber gives one concrete, date-driven run without changing the campaign or save version.
impact_assessment.benefits: Every local day maps to one of the 18 chambers. The title card shows today's chamber, today's best and the current streak; clearing it saves separately, updates a consecutive-day streak and offers Back to title or Play again. A fresh player sees a featured chamber without unlocking campaign shortcuts.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: adds a separate prism-relay.daily.v1 key, daily controls and a daily victory branch; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: new normalized daily record, campaign best/unlocks untouched; layout: a new title card must fit 390 and 320 without pushing the CTA off screen.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Pure daily-selection, streak, gap, replay, corrupt-save and pruning cases; a 390/320 title and victory probe; a real played daily clear and replay; campaign progress equality checks; the 18-level regression and full gates.
